  1. Show HN: Take Voyager 1 apart, down to a single memory chip

    • Education
    • Space

    234 points · 57 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 16:18 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — An interactive Voyager project that lets visitors explore the two spacecraft and their story, from the mission scale down to a memory-chip/bit view. The landing page shows current distance and signal-time figures and links to journey and repair narratives.

    Discussion — The project drew enthusiasm for its presentation, but a technically knowledgeable commenter alleged modeling and factual inaccuracies. The author said the work used NASA/JPL material, acknowledged that RTG fuel spheres should be paired and that the Sun detector was not named, and supplied source links. A separate exchange covered the uncertain cause of Voyager 1's memory failure and cited NASA's statement that it cannot be determined with certainty.

  2. Show HN: Type Fighter 2

    • Education
    • Games

    143 points · 70 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 11:11 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Type Fighter II is an arcade-styled touch-typing game with player selection, settings, credits, and a leaderboard visible from its start screen.

    Discussion — Players found it fun but requested keyboard-layout support (including Turkish Q and AZERTY), clearer controls, and an arcade/practice mode. A long thread debated teaching sequence: home-row drills and arbitrary letter combinations versus early use of common, meaningful words for motivation. One comment reported an SSL-certificate problem.

  3. New Evidence Shows School Phone Bans Are Gradually Improving Test Scores

    • Education

    1301 points · 645 comments · 17 Nov 2026, 11:45 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The New York Times article reported new evidence associating school phone bans with gradually improving test scores. Its account presented the findings as evidence rather than proof that bans alone caused the gains.

    Discussion — Commenters debated causality, implementation differences, parental expectations, enforcement, and whether phone restrictions address broader educational problems. Several asked how the studies handled confounders and uneven adoption.

  4. Carnegie Mellon is putting computer science courses on YouTube for free

    • Education

    2372 points · 331 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 20:43 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Carnegie Mellon’s CS Learn launched free full lecture series on YouTube in subjects including machine learning, systems, software construction, architectures, AI agents, and production ML. The site says self-paced courseware, instant-feedback lessons, badges, and AI tutoring are planned, with several courses scheduled for January 2027.

    Discussion — The project lead described a student-supported effort with human lecture review and invited course requests. Readers welcomed the access but discussed the limits of lecture-only learning, course licensing and attribution, and the role of structured exercises and feedback.

  5. Show HN: DeepSeek V3 in ~200 lines of pure Jax

    • AI
    • Education

    276 points · 30 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 15:04 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — A MIT-licensed, educational JAX reimplementation of selected DeepSeek-V3 ideas in about 190 lines: multi-head latent attention, DeepSeekMoE, bias-based expert balancing, and multi-token prediction. The repository documents a 36.2M-parameter run trained on 207 public-domain detective books on a 24GB MacBook Air M5, and publishes its checkpoint, data, tests, and reproduction instructions.

    Discussion — Readers praised the readable first-principles implementation and asked for a clearer inventory of what is omitted versus DeepSeek-V3. One commenter reported getting it running on an AMD RX 7600 XT with ROCm/JAX and contributed setup notes; others requested learning resources and CPU/C++ support.

  6. Ask HN: What are the most useful, concrete AI skills to independently learn?

    • AI
    • Education

    93 points · 54 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 06:56 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The Ask HN post asked which concrete AI skills a moderately technical person can learn independently through online material and experimentation to benefit economically from LLMs and agents.

    Discussion — Answers emphasized problem framing, domain knowledge, evaluation, automation, data handling, tool use, and building useful workflows rather than prompt tricks alone. People also recommended shipping small projects and learning where models fail.
